routes.description: Ground objective moral value in God's nature, duties in divine commands, and enduring accountability and significance in divine judgment.
routes.successCriteria: Show that secular alternatives cannot adequately ground intrinsic value, categorical obligation, morally significant agency, and accountability, while theism supplies each foundation.

motionBridge.description: God is necessary for the complete objective foundation of morality.

centralBridges.description: God's necessarily good nature grounds objective moral value and human worth.
Divine commands grounded in God's nature supply genuinely prescriptive moral duties.
Divine judgment reconciles morality with ultimate accountability and significance.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Naturalistic physicalism and determinism cannot preserve morally significant free agency.
Ultimate accountability resolves conflicts between prudential self-interest and moral reasons.

routes.description: Defend secular moral realism through objective categorical reasons, rational agency, and idealized agreement without requiring divine authorship or cosmic permanence.
routes.successCriteria: Provide a coherent secular basis for objective value and duty, answer the lawgiver and agency challenges, and show that temporal moral significance survives without ultimate cosmic accountability.

motionBridge.description: A secular moral realism can adequately ground morality without God.

centralBridges.description: Objective categorical reasons to avoid harm and provide help can be basic moral facts.
Rules chosen by perfectly rational bargainers behind a veil of ignorance provide an objective secular foundation.
Objective moral importance need not be eternal or cosmically consequential.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Reflective rational capacities distinguish moral agents from nonresponsible animals.
Moral reasons may outweigh prudential reasons even when the two conflict.

sections.title: Objective value and secular foundations
sections.rationale: This section tests the competing accounts of objective categorical reasons, intrinsic human worth, and the contractarian foundation offered for secular moral realism.

sections.title: Moral duties and the lawgiver challenge
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether genuine prescriptions require a personal commander or can arise from reason and idealized rational agreement.

sections.title: Rational agency and naturalism
sections.rationale: This section evaluates whether naturalism can distinguish responsible moral agents from animals and preserve morally significant choice.

sections.title: Accountability and temporal significance
sections.rationale: This section tests the inference from absent final judgment and cosmic permanence to moral irrelevance or insignificance.

sections.title: Morality and prudential self-interest
sections.rationale: This section isolates whether conflict between morality and prudence defeats secular normativity or merely leaves distinct reasons in competition.
